title: The beautiful factors
hook: faith, mindfulness, conscience, concern, non-greed, non-hate, balance

segments.voice: Yesterday, dullness and doubt: sloth, torpor, and a mind stuck at a fork. Your line: dull and doubtful. Did cold water or a look at the sky help? Day one thousand seventy-eight.

The manual could have called them the good factors. It calls them the beautiful ones, sobhana. All week this path has been naming what troubles a moment of mind: the four under every unwholesome moment, greed's family, aversion's family, dullness and doubt. A long list, and an honest one. Today the week closes by turning the cloth over. The manual sets down the other side, and it begins with seven of them.
screen: `NOT GOOD: BEAUTIFUL.` → `A WEEK OF TROUBLES.` → `TURN THE CLOTH OVER.`

segments.voice: First, faith, saddha. In the Questions of King Milinda, Nagasena gives faith a picture. A king's army crosses a stream and churns it to mud. The king is thirsty. A water-clearing gem is dropped in, the mud settles, and the water is fit to drink. Faith, in that picture, is less about believing hard and more about the mind settling clear. Second, mindfulness, sati: the mind that doesn't float off, that stays with what's here. Third and fourth come as a pair, and their shadows appeared earlier this week. Conscience, hiri: the inner pull of, this is beneath me. Concern, ottappa: care for what an act will do. The troubled four included shamelessness and recklessness. These are their exact opposites. In the Anguttara Nikaya, the Buddha calls this pair two bright qualities that protect the world. Then non-greed, alobha: the open hand. Non-hate, adosa: the friendly face that doesn't turn away. And balance, tatramajjhattata: evenness, a mind holding things without tipping. These seven, together with tomorrow's six pairs, the manual finds in every beautiful moment of mind. Look at what they're made of. Not rare peak experiences. A settled mind, a mind that stays, some self-respect, some care, an open hand, a friendly face, an even keel. The Dhammapada sums up the teaching in one verse, in Max Müller's words: "Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened." The beautiful factors are what that purifying looks like from inside, one moment at a time. So the week ends with both sides of the cloth in view. A moment can be colored by greed, envy, fog. A moment can be colored by faith, care and an open hand. The same knowing, a different dye.
screen: `FAITH CLEARS THE WATER.` · `CONSCIENCE AND CONCERN GUARD.` · `AN OPEN HAND, A FRIENDLY FACE.` · then, large: `SAME KNOWING, DIFFERENT DYE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: notice one beautiful factor. Sit, and let the breath settle. Then look for something beautiful in this moment, in the manual's sense. Maybe mindfulness: the mind staying with the breath. Maybe balance: a little evenness, nothing tipping. Maybe non-hate: someone comes to mind and the face doesn't turn away. Find one. Name it quietly, the way the troubled ones were named all week. Let it be as small as it is. Small still counts. The bell holds the time.
Sobhana. Beautiful: the manual's name for the factors that color a moment well. Today's word.
Your line: the beautiful. Today, catch one beautiful moment in someone else, a held door, a patient answer, and name the factor to yourself. Day one thousand seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Abhidhamma students learn the beautiful factors by their Pali names alongside the unwholesome ones, and some Theravada teachers call hiri and ottappa, conscience and concern, the guardians of the world.

pairs: faith: the gem that clears the water
concern: care for what an act will do

myth: the manual calls these 'the good factors'
it calls them sobhana, the beautiful.
conscience and concern are exact opposites of shamelessness and recklessness
the troubled four held the shadows; these are the light.
in Nagasena's picture, faith means believing without looking
he compares faith to a gem that clears muddy water so the king can drink.

fork.setup: you're the king. your army has churned the stream to mud, and you're thirsty. what clears the water?
options: wait a day for it to settle.
fork.reveal: in Nagasena's picture, the gem goes in and the mud settles. faith, he says, works like that in the mind.

original.note: Pali sobhana: beautiful, the manual's name for the factors on the bright side.

trapdoor: what you thought: beautiful factors are rare, lofty feelings.
what it means: faith, mindfulness, conscience, concern, an open hand, a friendly face and balance.
what a scholar hears: sobhana is wider than wholesome; the manual also calls resultant and functional consciousness beautiful when these factors are present.

notes: Week close (days 1072–1078): the hook looks back over the week's unwholesome factors and the teach returns to day 1072's cloth-and-dye image.

The seven named are the first seven beautiful universals; the remaining twelve (the six pairs) come on day 1079. 'These seven, together with tomorrow's six pairs, the manual finds in every beautiful moment' follows Abhidhammattha Sangaha ch. 2. Confirm.
Milindapanha: faith as the water-clearing gem of a universal monarch whose army has muddied a stream. Confirm the section number and details.
AN 2.9 paraphrased ('two bright qualities protect the world'). Confirm the citation.
